nodes.name: Proposition 4.2: Normality in odd bases
nodes.statement:
There exists a choice of $\mathcal K$ and $\pmb{\varepsilon}$ as in (2.1) and (2.2), for instance (2.11), with the following property. For $\mu = \mu[\mathcal K, \pmb{\varepsilon}]$ as in (2.3) and any odd integer $r \in \mathbb N \setminus \{1\}$, the following relation holds:  
\begin{equation} 
\sum_{N=1}^{\infty} N^{-3} \mathtt I(h; r, N) < \infty \quad \text{  where } \quad 
\mathtt I(h;r, N) := \sum_{v = 1}^{N} \sum_{u = 1}^{N} \bigl| \widehat{\mu}(hr^u(r^v-1)) \bigr|. 
\end{equation} 
As a result, by the Davenport-Erd\H{o}s-LeVeque criterion (Lemma 4.1) and for this choice of $\mathcal K, \pmb{\varepsilon}$,  
\[\text{$\mu = \mu[\mathcal K, \pmb{\varepsilon}]$-almost every $x$ is $r$-normal for every odd integer $r \geq 3$.} \] More precisely, $\mu$ is supported on $\mathscr N(\mathcal O, \cdot) \cap [0,1)$, the set of real numbers in $[0, 1)$ that are normal to every odd base.
